# M4: Research Assistant

Branch `feat/m4-research`, worktree `../nt-m4`. Read `STATUS.md` first.
Migration file: `supabase/migrations/20261120000100_research.sql`.

## Goal

An evidence-grounded literature assistant built on Europe PMC and PubMed. **It must work with no
paid AI provider and no LLM at all.** An optional local Ollama model can write nicer summaries.

It must never invent a citation. Every `[n]` marker in an answer must point to a document that
was actually retrieved, and the server checks this.

## Checklist

## Notes

### What was built

- **API** (`api/app/research/`): Europe PMC and NCBI E-utilities clients (retries on 429/5xx with
  backoff and `Retry-After`, timeouts, per-request `User-Agent`, `tool=neurotrack`, no email or
  user data, a process-wide NCBI limiter at 3 req/s or 10 with `NCBI_API_KEY`); one normalised
  `Reference` model, interleaved merge and PMID/DOI dedup with field back-filling; evidence labels
  from publication types; `ExtractiveProvider` (default, verbatim quotes) and `OllamaProvider`
  (only when `OLLAMA_URL` is set, falls back to extractive on failure or when nothing it wrote
  survives validation); `validate_answer`, which also rejects `[n]`/`[ref]` placeholders, DOIs,
  PMIDs and "et al." citations that are not among the retrieved sources. Routes
  `GET /research/search` and `POST /research/answer` require auth; partial upstream failure is
  reported in `failed_sources`, total failure is a 502. 80 pytest tests, all network mocked with
  `httpx.MockTransport` against recorded fixtures.
- **Database** (`20261120000100_research.sql`): `literature_references` (append-only cache, per
  user since the review, unique `pmid` and unique `doi` with default NULLS DISTINCT, at least one required, generated
  weighted tsvector + GIN index, select/insert for `authenticated` only, column-level insert grant),
  `saved_references` and `research_queries` (own rows only; only `note` is updatable), and
  `cache_literature_references(jsonb)` (security invoker, `on conflict do nothing` across both
  unique keys, returns cached ids).
- **Web** (`/research`, `/research/saved`): three tabs (Search literature with source filter, Ask a
  question, Search my library via `textSearch` websearch), reference cards (evidence badge,
  collapsible abstract, DOI/PubMed/Europe PMC links, save/unsave with a private note), cited answers
  with `[n]` links that scroll to, focus and highlight the source, provider, removed-sentence count
  and disclaimer, per-user query history with re-run and clear, shareable `?mode=&q=` URLs, and
  explicit loading/empty/partial-source/error states. Pure helpers in `src/lib/research/` with Jest
  tests; gated Playwright spec `e2e/research.spec.ts` (not run).
- **Docs**: `docs/research-assistant.md`.

### Deviations

- The previous builder's uncommitted API work was reviewed and kept, with fixes: a broken
  `parse_citations` test, the PubMed efetch fixture trimmed from 64 KB to 17 KB (reference lists
  cut), the User-Agent now set per request rather than relying on the client, and Europe PMC
  `<h4>` structured-abstract headings kept as `Label: ` so they are not quoted as part of a
  sentence (found with one live request).
- Caching goes through the `cache_literature_references` RPC rather than a PostgREST upsert: an
  upsert can target only one unique key and needs UPDATE privilege, which the brief forbids. The
  RPC runs as the caller, so the insert policy still applies.
- `research_queries` has an extra `mode` column (`search`/`answer`/`library`) so history entries
  can be re-run in the right tool.
- Extra API settings `RESEARCH_TIMEOUT_S`, `OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_S` and `OLLAMA_MODEL` (in
  `api/.env.example`). No new dependencies.
- Responses add `failed_sources` (search and answer) and `provider_note` (answer).
- NCBI recommends an `email` parameter; it is deliberately not sent (brief: no personal data).
- Library search is ordered by year, not `ts_rank` (PostgREST `textSearch` cannot rank).

### Not verified here

- The migration was validated by reading only (rule 3); it has not been applied.
- The UI was checked by `pnpm build`, typecheck and lint, not in a signed-in browser session, and
  the Playwright spec was not run (rule 5). The signed-in specs need the API, the migration and
  live access to Europe PMC and PubMed.

### Review

Independent review of `origin/main...HEAD` (citation integrity first, then security).

**Verified**

- Citation path end to end: `[n]` is 1-based into `AnswerResult.sources`, which is exactly the
  list the provider was given (`with_abstract[:max_sources]`, after dedup and interleave); the web
  app keeps that order (`cacheAndDecorate` maps in place) and renders markers from the structured
  `citations`, re-checked against the source count. `[0]`, out-of-range indices, `[n]`/`[ref]`,
  overreaching ranges, fabricated DOIs/PMIDs and unknown "et al." are dropped and counted.
- Every link on a card is built from upstream identifiers (`doi.org/<doi>`,
  `pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/<pmid>/`, `europepmc.org/...`); the stored `url` is used only when it
  starts with `https://europepmc.org/`. All external links have `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
  Titles and abstracts are rendered as React text; there is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
- Evidence labels are described as evidence type, not quality, in the API disclaimer, the UI and
  the docs.
- SSRF: upstream hosts and paths are constants; user input goes only into query parameters
  (`URLSearchParams` on the web side, httpx params on the API side). `OLLAMA_URL` comes only from
  settings. Query length (300), `limit` (1..25) and `max_sources` (1..8) are bounded on both
  sides; timeouts, 3 attempts and capped `Retry-After` are in place. No email, user id or token
  goes upstream. Both routes require auth; every Server Action checks the session and validates
  input with zod.
- SQL (read as Postgres 15): the generated tsvector uses `'english'::regconfig` (immutable), GIN
  index, NULLS DISTINCT unique keys, RLS on all three tables, `anon` revoked, column-level grants,
  `cache_literature_references` with `search_path = ''`, fully qualified names, execute revoked
  from `public`/`anon`, and `on conflict do nothing` (which tolerates duplicates within one batch).

**Fixed**

- HIGH, citation integrity: the extractive provider could quote an abstract sentence that carries
  the abstract's own reference number ("... in primates [1].") and append `[2]`; the validator
  then read it as citing *our* source 1 as well (misattribution). Such sentences are now skipped.
  The validator also rejects leftovers of nested or malformed markers (`[[1]]`, `[1a]`, `[^2]`).
  Tests added.
- HIGH, security/integrity: shared-cache poisoning. Any signed-in user could insert a fabricated
  reference (directly or through the RPC), including a fake title/abstract under a real PMID that
  would then win every later insert of it, and other users would see it in their library and
  saved list. `literature_references` now records `inserted_by` (default `auth.uid()`), RLS limits
  select/insert to the owner, PMID/DOI are unique per user, and saving requires the reference to
  be the user's own row (a foreign key alone ignores RLS). A user can only mislead themselves.
  Displayed search results and answer sources always come from the API response, never from the
  cache. Docs and UI wording updated ("Search my library" is now literally the user's own
  retrieved references). Deviation from the brief's "shared cache": a shared cache needs a trusted
  writer, which NeuroTrack does not have.
- MEDIUM: the process-wide NCBI limiter queue was unbounded, so a burst could make every later
  PubMed call sleep without limit. It now fails fast (PubMed reported in `failed_sources`) when the
  next slot is more than 10 s away.
- LOW: `TooManyRedirects`/`DecodingError` escaped as a 500; all `httpx.RequestError`s are now
  retried and reported as a failed source.

**Left open**

- MEDIUM: with Ollama, validation proves provenance, not support: a sentence can cite a retrieved
  source that does not say what the sentence claims, and the model's choice of section
  ("Established findings") is not checked. Documented in Limitations; extractive (default) is
  verbatim.
- LOW: the NCBI limiter is per process; running the API with several workers multiplies the rate.
  Run one worker or set `NCBI_API_KEY`.
- LOW: the outbound client follows redirects (hosts are fixed HTTPS constants, so the risk is
  small).
- LOW: `parseMarkedText` in `src/lib/research/citations.ts` is unused (tested only) and does not
  understand ranges; harmless while unused.
- The migration is still validated by reading only, and the Playwright spec has not been run.

All checks green after the fixes: `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`
(111), `pnpm build`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `pytest` (88). `pnpm api:types` shows no
drift.
